about.text: In this lesson you arrange a meeting at work. You suggest a time, say no politely and say what you think will happen. Then the plan changes, so you move the meeting.
goals: Fix a time: Are you free on Monday? How about Tuesday?
Say no politely: I'm afraid I can't. I'm meeting a customer.
Talk about the future: I'm meeting her at ten. I'm going to book a room. I think it'll be busy.
Read a message thread, and write a message to move a meeting.
Arrange a meeting with two people, then move it when something changes.

chapters.title: Fixing a time
chapters.text:
In this lesson you make plans with other people. Then you change them.
First, you listen to two colleagues, Mei and Carlos. They need an hour next week to plan a training day.
Mei asks: Are you free on Monday morning? Carlos looks at his diary.
He says: I'm afraid I can't. The words I'm afraid make a no polite.
Then Mei suggests another time: How about Tuesday afternoon?
When they agree, Carlos says the day, the time and the place again. That is a good way to check.

chapters.title: Arranged, decided, or a guess
chapters.text:
This lesson has three ways to talk about the future.
One: a plan with a day or a time, and another person knows about it. Use am, is or are, and a verb with -ing. I'm meeting a customer at ten.
Two: something you decided, but did not arrange. Use going to. I'm going to book a room.
Three: a guess. You think it, but you don't know it. Use will. I think it'll be busy.
With a guess, say how sure you are. Definitely means very sure. Probably means nearly sure. Perhaps means not sure.

chapters.title: A message thread
chapters.text:
Next, you read a message thread from a team at work. Four people try to find a time for one meeting.
The first day does not suit everyone. One person is on leave, so they move the meeting.
Read it once, and find the day they choose. Then read it again, slowly, for the times.
Then you write a message to move a meeting. Say sorry, give the reason, and suggest two new times.

chapters.title: Arrange it, then move it
chapters.text:
In the task, you arrange a meeting with two colleagues, Kwame and Lena. Everybody has a busy week.
Ask: Are you free on Wednesday? Suggest a time: How about three o'clock? If you can't come, say so politely.
When you all agree, say the plan back: Wednesday at three, in Room 2.
Then something changes. Say sorry, give the reason, and find a new time.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a story or an article about plans.
Look at the title first, and predict what will happen. Make a guess with will.
Then read it once for the main idea. Read it again to answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You need to meet a colleague next week. How do you find a time?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people send a message first. For a quick question, it is often faster to go to their desk.

conversation.title: Are you free on Monday?
conversation.setting: Mei and Carlos work in the same office. Mei is planning a training day for new staff. She needs an hour with Carlos next week, so she stops at his desk.
lines: Hi, Carlos. Have you got a minute? It's about the training day.
I'm going to invite all the new staff. We need an hour to plan it.
OK. Let me look at my diary.
Are you free on Monday morning?
I'm afraid I can't. I'm meeting a customer at ten.
Sorry, I'm working at the other office on Tuesday. What about Wednesday instead?
Wednesday is busy for me, but I've got a spare hour at two.
Two o'clock suits me. Where shall we meet?
In Room 3. It'll probably be quiet after lunch.
Good. So, that's Wednesday at two, in Room 3.
That's right. I think it'll be a great training day!
Definitely. I'll put it in my diary now.

questions.q: Why can't Carlos meet on Monday morning?
wrong: He's working at the other office.
He's going to be on holiday.
questions.why: Carlos says: I'm afraid I can't. I'm meeting a customer at ten.

questions.q: When and where are they going to meet?
questions.a: on Wednesday at two, in Room 3
wrong: on Monday at ten, at Carlos's desk
questions.why: Carlos says it back: So, that's Wednesday at two, in Room 3.

questions.q: What has Mei decided to do?
questions.why: Mei says: I'm going to invite all the new staff.

phrases.use: Asking a colleague for a short talk.

phrases.text: Let me look at my diary.
phrases.use: Saying you will check your plans first.

phrases.text: Are you free on Monday morning?
phrases.use: Asking if someone can meet at a time.
Saying no politely. I'm afraid makes it softer.
Saying yes: the time is good for you.

phrases.text: So, that's Wednesday at two, in Room 3.
phrases.use: Saying the plan again, to check it.

items.meaning: Free at a time, so you can meet, work or help. A room can be available too.
items.example: Are you available on Thursday morning?

items.meaning: A plan that you make with another person: a day, a time and a place.
items.example: We have an arrangement to meet on Friday at ten.

items.meaning: A small book or an app where you write your plans and appointments.
items.example: Let me look at my diary.

items.meaning: A plan that shows what happens and when.
items.example: My schedule is very full this week.

items.meaning: To give an idea or a plan, so other people can think about it.
items.example: Can I suggest Thursday at two?

items.meaning: In the place of another person or thing.
items.example: I can't do Monday. Can we meet on Tuesday instead?

items.meaning: To give something and get something back. Two people can swap shifts, days or seats.
items.example: Can we swap shifts next week? I've got an appointment.

items.meaning: Free and not used, so you can use it for something else.
items.example: I've got a spare hour after lunch.

items.meaning: To be good or right for someone, like a time, a day or a plan.
items.example: Does ten o'clock suit you?

items.meaning: Nearly sure. You think yes, but you don't know.
items.example: The meeting will probably finish at four.

items.meaning: Maybe. It can happen, but you are not sure.
items.example: Perhaps Omar can come too.

items.meaning: For sure. There is no question about it.
items.example: I'll definitely be there at nine.

items.meaning: To think that something will happen.
items.example: I expect the trains will be busy on Friday.

items.meaning: To say now what you think will happen later.
items.example: Nobody can predict the traffic on a Friday.

sound.title: can and can't
sound.explain: In British English, can't is long and strong. It has the sound in car and park. In a sentence, can is short and quiet: I can come. So listen for the long sound. It tells you the answer is no. Listen, then say each group.
groups: I can come · I can meet · we can talk
lines: I can't do Monday, but I can do Tuesday.

sayIt.instructions: Say Carlos's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Is your can't long and clear?
lines: I'm afraid I can't. I'm meeting a customer at ten.
Sorry, I'm working at the other office on Tuesday. What about Wednesday instead?
Two o'clock suits me. Where shall we meet?
Good. So, that's Wednesday at two, in Room 3.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Two are plans with a day or a time. One is a decision. One is a guess.
examples: I'm meeting a customer at ten.
I'm working at the other office on Tuesday.
I'm going to invite all the new staff.
It'll probably be quiet after lunch.
spot.question: Which two are plans with a time? Which one is a decision? Which one is a guess? Look at the verbs.
spot.answer: Plans with a time: I'm meeting, I'm working. They use am, is or are + -ing, and a day or a time. The decision uses going to: I'm going to invite. The guess uses will: it'll probably be quiet. Mei thinks so, but she doesn't know.

rules.title: I'm meeting her on Tuesday: a plan with a time
rule: A plan with a time, and other people know about it: am, is, are + -ing.
I'm meeting a customer at ten. We're having lunch on Friday.
No: I'm not working on Friday. Ask: What are you doing on Thursday?
Ask for a time: Are you free on Monday? How about Tuesday?
Say no politely: I'm afraid I can't. I'm visiting a customer.
rules.mistake: Not: I meeting her on Tuesday. Say: I'm meeting her on Tuesday.

rules.title: Going to for decisions, will for guesses
rule: You decided before: am, is, are + going to + a verb. I'm going to book a room.
A guess about the future: will + a verb. I think it'll be busy.
How sure? definitely (very sure), probably (nearly sure), perhaps (not sure).
Word order: It'll probably rain. It definitely won't rain. Perhaps it'll rain.
No: It won't be busy. (won't = will not) I'm not going to wait.
rules.mistake: Not: I going to book a room. Say: I'm going to book a room.

practice.q: Sorry, I can't come on Monday. ___ a customer at ten.
practice.why: A plan with a time: I'm + a verb + -ing.

practice.q: What ___ you doing on Friday evening?
practice.why: Asking about a plan: What are you doing …?

practice.q: Omar ___ working on Saturday. He's got the day off.
practice.why: No, with a plan: is not + -ing. He isn't working.

practice.q: I've decided. ___ look for a new job this year.
practice.why: A decision: I'm going to + a verb.

options: I think the meeting will be long.
I'm going to book a room.
practice.a: I think the meeting will be long.
practice.why: A guess uses will: I think … will be long.

practice.q: Take an umbrella. It ___ rain this afternoon.
practice.why: A guess: will + probably + a verb.

practice.q: It ___ rain tomorrow. My phone says sun all day.
practice.why: A guess, with no: won't = will not.

practice.q: I'm not sure, but ___ Samir can come too.
practice.why: You are not sure, so perhaps.

practice.q: I can't do Thursday. Can we meet on Friday ___ ?
practice.why: Instead: in the place of Thursday.

yourTurn.prompt: Write about your next week. Write two plans with a day or a time. Then write one decision with going to, and one guess with will.
yourTurn.model: On Monday I'm starting work at seven. On Thursday evening I'm meeting my sister for dinner. I'm going to clean my flat on Saturday. I think it'll probably rain at the weekend.

text.title: Finding a time for one meeting
text.body:
Sales team · messages
Mon 09:10 · Dani: Morning, all. We need to look at the March sales numbers this week. Shall we meet on Thursday?
Mon 09:25 · Sara: Thursday suits me. What time?
Mon 09:30 · Dani: How about 2 pm? I'm going to book Room 2.
Mon 10:05 · Joel: I'm afraid Thursday is impossible for me. I'm visiting the Hillford office all day. Is Friday morning possible?
Mon 10:20 · Sara: Friday morning is fine for me too.
Mon 14:40 · Dani: OK, let's postpone it to Friday at 10. I'll confirm the room this afternoon.
Tue 08:55 · Priya: Sorry, I've only just seen this. I'm on leave on Friday. Is Thursday still possible?
Tue 09:20 · Joel: Sorry, Thursday still doesn't work for me.
Tue 09:45 · Dani: Then let's stay with Friday at 10. Priya, send me your numbers, and I'll forward you the notes after the meeting.
Tue 16:30 · Dani: Room 2 is booked for Friday at 10. It's in everyone's calendar now. I'll send a reminder on Thursday.

gist.a: finding a time for a team meeting
gist.why: Dani asks: Shall we meet on Thursday? Then the team looks for a time.

gist.q: When is the meeting in the end?
gist.why: Dani's last message says: Room 2 is booked for Friday at 10.

detail.q: Why can't Joel come on Thursday?
detail.why: Joel says: I'm visiting the Hillford office all day.

detail.q: Why does Priya ask about Thursday?
detail.why: Priya says: I'm on leave on Friday. Is Thursday still possible?

detail.q: How will Priya find out about the meeting?
detail.a: Dani will forward her the notes.
wrong: Sara will phone her on Friday.
She will join the meeting for an hour.
detail.why: Dani says: I'll forward you the notes after the meeting.

detail.q: What will Dani do on Thursday?
detail.why: Dani's last message says: I'll send a reminder on Thursday.

items.meaning: To move something to a later day or time.
items.example: Let's postpone the meeting until next week.

items.meaning: To say or write that a plan is now sure.
items.example: Can you confirm the time by email?

items.meaning: A message that helps you remember something.
items.example: My phone sends me a reminder an hour before a meeting.

items.meaning: To say sorry. It is a little more formal than sorry.
items.example: I apologise for the late reply.

items.meaning: To send an email or a message that you got to another person.
items.example: Can you forward me Dani's email?

items.meaning: To change the day or the time of a plan.
items.example: Can we rearrange our meeting for Friday?

items.meaning: It can happen, or you can do it.
items.example: Is it possible to meet on Monday?

items.meaning: It cannot happen, or you cannot do it.
items.example: Thursday is impossible for me. I'm away all day.

items.meaning: Away from work for a time that you planned, for example on holiday.
items.example: Priya is on leave until Monday.

items.meaning: A page or an app that shows the days and months. At work, it shows your meetings.
items.example: I'll put the meeting in my calendar.

model.title: A message to move a meeting
model.body:
Hi Samir,
I'm very sorry, but I need to rearrange our meeting on Thursday at 3.
My manager is sending me to a training day that afternoon.
Are you available on Friday morning? Or how about Monday at 10?
I apologise for the change. I'll send a new calendar invitation when you reply.
Best wishes,
Amina

write.task: You have an arrangement to meet a colleague, but now you can't go. Write a message to move the meeting. Say sorry, give the reason, and suggest two new times. It can be real or made up.
write.starter: Hi …, I'm very sorry, but I need to rearrange …
checklist: I said which meeting: the day and the time.
I gave a reason with -ing: I'm meeting …, I'm working …
I suggested two new times: Are you available …? How about …?
I said sorry: I'm sorry, or I apologise.

card.title: One meeting, three busy people
card.situation: You need one hour next week with two colleagues, Kwame and Lena. You are planning a new project. Everybody's schedule is full. Kwame is visiting customers on Monday and Tuesday. Lena is on a training course on Wednesday morning.
card.goal: Find a time that suits all three of you, and say it back to check. Then something changes. Say sorry, and move the meeting to a new time.

phrases: Are you both free on Monday?
I'm afraid I can't. I'm visiting customers.
How about Wednesday afternoon, at three?
So, that's Wednesday at three, in Room 2.
I'm very sorry, but I need to rearrange our meeting.
prepare.notes: Make notes first. Write two things you are doing next week, with a day and a time. Then write two times when you are free.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher and a classmate are Kwame and Lena. Find a time together, and say it back. Then your teacher changes something, and you move the meeting.
doIt.wehel: You are two of my colleagues, Kwame and Lena. We need one hour next week to plan a project. Kwame is busy on Monday and Tuesday. Lena is busy on Wednesday morning. Help me find a time, and ask me to say it back. Then tell me that something has changed, so I have to move the meeting. Use simple English.

model.title: Fixing the meeting, and moving it
lines: Hi, both. We need an hour next week for the new project. Are you free on Monday?
I'm afraid I can't. I'm visiting customers on Monday and Tuesday.
Sorry, I'm on a training course on Wednesday morning. The afternoon suits me.
Wednesday afternoon is fine for me too. How about three o'clock?
Great. So, that's Wednesday at three, in Room 2.
Perfect. I'll put it in my calendar.
Hi Kwame and Lena, I'm very sorry, but my manager needs me on Wednesday afternoon. Can we rearrange?
No problem. Is Thursday at ten possible?
Thursday at ten is fine. I'm working from home, but I can come in.
Thank you both. So, Thursday at ten, in Room 2. I'll send you a reminder.
compare: Did you ask with Are you free on …? and suggest with How about …?
Did you say no politely with I'm afraid I can't, and give a reason?
Did you say the day, the time and the place back to check?
When the plan changed, did you say sorry and suggest a new time?

canDo: I can ask if someone is free, and suggest a time.
I can say no politely and suggest another time.
I can talk about the future: plans with -ing, going to and will.
I can read a message thread and write a message to move a meeting.
I can arrange a meeting with two people, and move it when something changes.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. What are the people planning? What do you think will happen?
reading.talk: Did the plans in the story work? What are you doing next weekend, and what are you going to do? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: We ___ lunch with a customer on Friday. It's in my diary.
quiz.why: A plan with a time: we are + -ing.

quiz.q: Are you free on Monday? — I'm ___ I can't. I'm working late.
quiz.why: I'm afraid I can't is a polite no.

quiz.q: Wednesday at two? Yes, that ___ me.
quiz.why: That suits me: that time is good for me.

quiz.q: I think the new café ___ very busy.
quiz.why: A guess: I think + will + a verb.

quiz.q: I've decided. I'm ___ ask my manager for a day off.
quiz.why: A decision: I'm going to + a verb.

quiz.q: Priya isn't at work this week. She's ___ .
quiz.why: On leave: away from work for a planned time.

quiz.q: I'm ill today. Can we ___ the meeting to next week?
quiz.why: Postpone: move it to a later time.

quiz.q: You ___ wear a uniform. Your own clothes are fine.
quiz.why: There is no rule, so don't have to.

quiz.q: Would you like ___ join us for lunch?
quiz.why: Would you like + to + a verb.

quiz.q: I haven't posted the letter ___ . I'll do it after lunch.
quiz.why: Not … yet: it hasn't happened, but it will.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the conversation in pairs. Then change the days and the reasons. Each learner says no once with I'm afraid I can't, and suggests another time.
Day 2: a diary game. Each learner writes a made-up week with four plans. In pairs, they ask What are you doing on …? Then each learner says one decision with going to and one guess with will.
Day 3: the task. Learners arrange a meeting with you and a classmate, and say it back. Then you change something, and they move the meeting.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and read two learners' messages to move a meeting aloud.
